NAXOS - ZERFALL UND GESTALTUNG

1 - NAXOS-GESTALTEN
Hinter den Mauern der ehemaligen Naxos-Fabrikhallen eröffnete sich eine ganz eigene Welt. Wer entsprechend offen war, der traf queere Rabbits, die lächelnden City-Ghosts oder eine Alice, die fantasievoll ihr Wunderland gestaltete. In anderen Bereichen waren es surreale Buchstaben, die ein Eigenleben entwickelten, und Mondsterne, die in Einkaufswagen tanzten, oder auch seltsame, scheinbar körperlose Gesichter, die für einen kurzen Moment im Licht einer Taschenlampe sichtbar waren, um dann wieder im Dunkel der Räume zu verschwinden. All diese Gestalten der zerfallenen Naxos-Hallen waren auf der Suche nach Wirklichkeitsnischen, in denen sie existieren konnten - und sie waren fündig geworden.

2 - DIE GESCHICHTE DER NAXOS-UNION
In der Geschichte der Naxos-Union spiegelten sich nachhaltig die Polaritäten eines kapitalistischen Wirtschaftssystems. Der Naxos-Union gelang der Aufstieg zu einem weltweit führenden Unternehmen, das später jedoch an veränderten Produktionsbedingungen zerbrach. Die in Frankfurt am Main beheimatete Firma sicherte sich die Rechte für den Abbau eines besonderen Schmirgelgesteins auf der griechischen Insel Naxos und begann um 1880 mit der über Jahrzehnte hinweg äußerst profitablen Produktion von Schleifmaschinen. Erst in den achtziger Jahren des letzten Jahrhunderts verlor das Unternehmen rapide an Bedeutung. Die Besitzverhältnisse wandelten sich mehrfach und die ursprünglichen Produktionsstätten in Frankfurt wurden aufgegeben. Ihre dunkelste Zeit erlebte die Naxos-Union im Zuge der faschistischen Terrorherrschaft, als der Betrieb vor allem durch den Einsatz von ZwangsarbeiterInnen aufrecht erhalten wurde.

3 - DIE NAXOS-GEBÄUDE
Das ehemalige Gelände der Naxos-Union an der Wittelsbacherallee in Frankfurt unterteilte sich nach dem Niedergang des Unternehmens in drei Bereiche. Ein ehemaliges großes Verwaltungsgebäude und die im mittleren Bereich liegende ehemalige Produktionshalle wurden in mehreren Etappen saniert und werden von Agenturen bzw. Theater- und Kunstprojekten genutzt. Die mittlere Halle ist inzwischen auf Grund ihrer architektonischen bzw. historischen Bedeutung als ein Denkmal der Industriekultur geschützt. Der dritte Gebäudekomplex mit mehreren Hallen und einem weiteren Verwaltungsgebäude stand über viele Jahre hinweg weitgehend leer und verfiel zunehmend. Gleichzeitig entwickelte er sich trotz Verbote und Absperrungen als ein Freiraum für zahlreiche KünstlerInnen, welche die Räumlichkeiten kreativ gestalteten und immer wieder mit neuem Leben erfüllten. Nachdem die Stadt Frankfurt Teile des Geländes zu einem völlig überhöhten Preis über Jahre hinweg gemietet hatte, erwarb sie 2006 das gesamte Grundstück. Inzwischen wurden die leer stehenden Hallen vollständig abgerissen. Zukünftig sollen dort verschiedene Wohnprojekte einen Platz finden.

4 - NAXOS ALS KREATIVER FREIRAUM
Die Kunst der Metropolen findet sich kaum in den herkömmlichen Galerien und Museen. Sie wird erst dann wirklich sichtbar und verständlich, wenn man sich vom bürgerlichen Kunstbegriff löst und auf die Straßen begibt. Ganze Stadtteile sind zu Museen einer urbanen Kultur des Undergrounds geworden, die in den letzten Jahrzehnten in den vielfältigen Ausformungen der Streetart einen kreativen Ausdruck gefunden hat. Allerdings bleibt sie überall dort, wo es nur um die penetrante Markierung mit dem eigenen Namenzug oder ein Bekritzeln freier Flächen geht, in egozentrischen und destruktiven Sackgassen verfangen. Ihr konstruktives Potential entfaltet die Streetart als Wiederaneignung öffentlichen Raumes stattdessen überall dort, wo sie kritische Impulse gibt und positive Energien freisetzt. In diesem Sinne veränderte sich zeitweise die Bedeutung der Naxos-Hallen und sie wurden als kreativer Freiraum zu einem Museum des Untergrunds, das die Naxos-Gestalten mit Leben erfüllten.

Wolfgang Sterneck, April 2011.
www.sterneck.net

Title: Occupy Wall Street 2
Description:
Frank Fullard posted a photo:

No 23 of 100 Strangers

I met up with Bill Scott among the protestors at the Occupy Wall Street demonstration. It transpires that he is a Professor of English at Pittsburgh University. One of his areas of special interest is how working class people have been depicted in American literature. However, I formed the opinion that his presence on the protest was not about satisfying any academic interest he might have. I feel he was there because he believes in what the protesters are trying to achieve in terms of bringing about real change in American society.

As it happens he has his first book published later this week. It is called “Troublemakers: Power, Representation, and the Fiction of the Mass Worker” and is available on Amazon. I suspect the OWS protests will create some trouble for part of the US establishment, but the irony is that I cannot imagine meeting a more mild-mannered protester, troublemaker if you prefer, than Bill.

For having the courage of his convictions Bill Scott becomes No.23 in my 100 Strangers portfolio

To see others in my 100 Strangers group go to www.flickr.com/photos/frankfullard/sets/72157624950918492/

Description:
pete riches posted a photo:

 

#OccupyLSX protesters gather at St. Paul's Cathedral - Day One, 15.10.2011


As part of the newly-emerging global "Occupy" movement which has seen a continuous occupation of Liberty Park near Wall Street in New York, and which today saw protests in approximately 950 cities worldwide against the corruption of both bankers and governments, around 4-5,000 activists - having been blocked by police from their original objective, Paternoster Square which leads to the London Stock Exchange - converged on the front steps of St. Paul's Cathedral in the City of London to begin an occupation which. it is hoped, will oblige the financiers and bankers to realise that there are real people being grievously punished for the unpunished crimes of the banking industry which have resulted in crashing world economies and swingeing 'austerity measures' which are only paid for by the poor and middle classes. In the meanwhile the entire country has been treated to the disgraceful sight of the very people who caused this unmitigated shitstorm of greed, dishonesty and arrogance having the audacity to reward themselves with millions of pounds in bonuses, despite almost bringing the world economy to its knees.

Throughout the day the completely peaceful protesters discussed their grievances and through a series of open Spanish-style 'congresses' or 'people's assemblies' formulated a series of propositions which form the basis of the mass protest.

During the afternoon the crowd was joined by Wikileaks founder Julian Assange who arrived wearing the obligatory Guy Fawkes mask made famous in the cult film "V for Vendetta", which is worn by members of hacktivist group Anonymous. Assange, wearing an electronic tag on his leg imposed by the British court as he is under house arrest awaiting deportation to Sweden - was accompanied by two police detectives, one of whom frequently made a point of holding Assange's shoulder, as if they thought for one second that one of the most identifiable faces in the world right now would ever be able to make a run for it, surrounded completely by a cordon of upwards of 3-400 police.

The only mindless, vindictive violence came from some members of the Territorial Support Group who were militaristic in their brutality towards completely passive citizens when they decided to rush the steps of the cathedral once darkness fell, during which assault they stamped on people's heads and bodies, punched and kicked several people and were seen to rip the hijab off one girl's head. All of this was to prove or gain nothing whatsoever strategically except the ability of the police to be - in my opinion as I watched it from very close quarters - criminally, dangerously violent to passive, peaceful protesters who no longer, it seems, are protected from violence by the agents of the State. When the police commit violence everyone - especially the police - knows it is very difficult to go after them to demand legal justice.

Several hours later the police abandoned the steps at the request of Cathedral officials, leaving everyone to wonder what was the primary motive of the senior officer who gave the order to lead this attack on private land when no crime had been committed. This was Abuse of Process in many people's opinion.

In the meanwhile the entire country has been treated to the disgraceful sight of the very people who caused this unmitigated shitstorm of greed, dishonesty and arrogance having the audacity to reward themselves with millions of pounds in bonuses, despite almost bringing the world economy to its knees.

Throughout the day the completely peaceful protesters discussed their grievances and through a series of open Spanish-style 'congresses' or 'people's assemblies' formulated a series of propositions which form the basis of the mass protest.

During the afternoon the crowd was joined by Wikileaks founder Julian Assange who arrived wearing the obligatory Guy Fawkes mask made famous in the cult film "V for Vendetta", which is worn by members of hacktivist group Anonymous. Assange, wearing an electronic tag on his leg imposed by the British court as he is under house arrest awaiting deportation to Sweden - was accompanied by two police detectives, one of whom frequently made a point of holding Assange's shoulder, as if they thought for one second that one of the most identifiable faces in the world right now would ever be able to make a run for it, surrounded completely by a cordon of upwards of 3-400 police.

The only mindless, vindictive violence came from some members of the Territorial Support Group who were militaristic in their brutality towards completely passive citizens when they decided to rush the steps of the cathedral once darkness fell, during which assault they stamped on people's heads and bodies, punched and kicked several people and were seen to rip the hijab off one girl's head. All of this was to prove or gain nothing whatsoever strategically except the ability of the police to be - in my opinion as I watched it from very close quarters - criminally, dangerously violent to passive, peaceful protesters who no longer, it seems, are protected from violence by the agents of the State. When the police commit violence everyone - especially the police - knows it is very difficult to go after them to demand legal justice.

Several hours later the police abandoned the steps at the request of Cathedral officials, leaving everyone to wonder what was the primary motive of the senior officer who gave the order to lead this attack on private land when no crime had been committed. This was Abuse of Process in many people's opinion.

In the meanwhile the entire country has been treated to the disgraceful sight of the very people who caused this unmitigated shitstorm of greed, dishonesty and arrogance having the audacity to reward themselves with millions of pounds in bonuses, despite almost bringing the world economy to its knees.

As part of the newly-emerging global "Occupy" movement which has seen a continuous occupation of Liberty Park near Wall Street in New York, and which today saw protests in approximately 950 cities worldwide against the corruption of both bankers and governments, around 4-5,000 activists - having been blocked by police from their original objective, Paternoster Square which leads to the London Stock Exchange - converged on the front steps of St. Paul's Cathedral in the City of London to begin an occupation which. it is hoped, will oblige the financiers and bankers to realise that there are real people being grievously punished for the unpunished crimes of the banking industry which have resulted in crashing world economies and swingeing 'austerity measures' which are only paid for by the poor and middle classes. In the meanwhile the entire country has been treated to the disgraceful sight of the very people who caused this unmitigated shitstorm of greed, dishonesty and arrogance having the audacity to reward themselves with millions of pounds in bonuses, despite almost bringing the world economy to its knees.

Throughout the day the completely peaceful protesters discussed their grievances and through a series of open Spanish-style 'congresses' or 'people's assemblies' formulated a series of propositions which form the basis of the mass protest.

During the afternoon the crowd was joined by Wikileaks founder Julian Assange who arrived wearing the obligatory Guy Fawkes mask made famous in the cult film "V for Vendetta", which is worn by members of hacktivist group Anonymous. Assange, wearing an electronic tag on his leg imposed by the British court as he is under house arrest awaiting deportation to Sweden - was accompanied by two police detectives, one of whom frequently made a point of holding Assange's shoulder, as if they thought for one second that one of the most identifiable faces in the world right now would ever be able to make a run for it, surrounded completely by a cordon of upwards of 3-400 police.

The only mindless, vindictive violence came from some members of the Territorial Support Group who were militaristic in their brutality towards completely passive citizens when they decided to rush the steps of the cathedral once darkness fell, during which assault they stamped on people's heads and bodies, punched and kicked several people and were seen to rip the hijab off one girl's head. All of this was to prove or gain nothing whatsoever strategically except the ability of the police to be - in my opinion as I watched it from very close quarters - criminally, dangerously violent to passive, peaceful protesters who no longer, it seems, are protected from violence by the agents of the State. When the police commit violence everyone - especially the police - knows it is very difficult to go after them to demand legal justice.

Several hours later the police abandoned the steps at the request of Cathedral officials, leaving everyone to wonder what was the primary motive of the senior officer who gave the order to lead this attack on private land when no crime had been committed. This was Abuse of Process in many people's opinion.

As part of the newly-emerging global "Occupy" movement which has seen a continuous occupation of Liberty Park near Wall Street in New York, and which today saw protests in approximately 950 cities worldwide against the corruption of both bankers and governments, around 4-5,000 activists - having been blocked by police from their original objective, Paternoster Square which leads to the London Stock Exchange - converged on the front steps of St. Paul's Cathedral in the City of London to begin an occupation which. it is hoped, will oblige the financiers and bankers to realise that there are real people being grievously punished for the unpunished crimes of the banking industry which have resulted in crashing world economies and swingeing 'austerity measures' which are only paid for by the poor and middle classes. In the meanwhile the entire country has been treated to the disgraceful sight of the very people who caused this unmitigated shitstorm of greed, dishonesty and arrogance having the audacity to reward themselves with millions of pounds in bonuses, despite almost bringing the world economy to its knees.

Throughout the day the completely peaceful protesters discussed their grievances and through a series of open Spanish-style 'congresses' or 'people's assemblies' formulated a series of propositions which form the basis of the mass protest.

During the afternoon the crowd was joined by Wikileaks founder Julian Assange who arrived wearing the obligatory Guy Fawkes mask made famous in the cult film "V for Vendetta", which is worn by members of hacktivist group Anonymous. Assange, wearing an electronic tag on his leg imposed by the British court as he is under house arrest awaiting deportation to Sweden - was accompanied by two police detectives, one of whom frequently made a point of holding Assange's shoulder, as if they thought for one second that one of the most identifiable faces in the world right now would ever be able to make a run for it, surrounded completely by a cordon of upwards of 3-400 police.

The only mindless, vindictive violence came from some members of the Territorial Support Group who were militaristic in their brutality towards completely passive citizens when they decided to rush the steps of the cathedral once darkness fell, during which assault they stamped on people's heads and bodies, punched and kicked several people and were seen to rip the hijab off one girl's head. All of this was to prove or gain nothing whatsoever strategically except the ability of the police to be - in my opinion as I watched it from very close quarters - criminally, dangerously violent to passive, peaceful protesters who no longer, it seems, are protected from violence by the agents of the State. When the police commit violence everyone - especially the police - knows it is very difficult to go after them to demand legal justice.

Several hours later the police abandoned the steps at the request of Cathedral officials, leaving everyone to wonder what was the primary motive of the senior officer who gave the order to lead this attack on private land when no crime had been committed. This was Abuse of Process in many people's opinion.

Throughout the day the completely peaceful protesters discussed their grievances and through a series of open Spanish-style 'congresses' or 'people's assemblies' formulated a series of propositions which form the basis of the mass protest.

During the afternoon the crowd was joined by Wikileaks founder Julian Assange who arrived wearing the obligatory Guy Fawkes mask made famous in the cult film "V for Vendetta", which is worn by members of hacktivist group Anonymous. Assange, wearing an electronic tag on his leg imposed by the British court as he is under house arrest awaiting deportation to Sweden - was accompanied by two police detectives, one of whom frequently made a point of holding Assange's shoulder, as if they thought for one second that one of the most identifiable faces in the world right now would ever be able to make a run for it, surrounded completely by a cordon of upwards of 3-400 police.

The only mindless, vindictive violence came from some members of the Territorial Support Group who were militaristic in their brutality towards completely passive citizens when they decided to rush the steps of the cathedral once darkness fell, during which assault they stamped on people's heads and bodies, punched and kicked several people and were seen to rip the hijab off one girl's head. All of this was to prove or gain nothing whatsoever strategically except the ability of the police to be - in my opinion as I watched it from very close quarters - criminally, dangerously violent to passive, peaceful protesters who no longer, it seems, are protected from violence by the agents of the State. When the police commit violence everyone - especially the police - knows it is very difficult to go after them to demand legal justice.

Several hours later the police abandoned the steps at the request of Cathedral officials, leaving everyone to wonder what was the primary motive of the senior officer who gave the order to lead this attack on private land when no crime had been committed. This was Abuse of Process in many people's opinion.

To follow the progress of #OccupyLSX and #OccupyLondon visit their website here, and follow them on Twitter HERE and HERE.

To follow the progress of the second protest camp set up in Finsbury Square on 22.10.2011 (photos soon) visit BeyondClicktivism and follow them on Twitter

Title: Occupy Wall Street
Description:
Hell's Attik posted a photo:

October 3, 2011

Occupy Wall Street is an ongoing series of demonstrations initiated by the Canadian activist group Adbusters in New York City, headquartered in Zuccotti Park in the Wall Street financial district, protesting social and economic inequality, corporate greed, corporate power and influence over government (particularly from the financial services sector), and of lobbyists.

The original protest began on September 17, 2011, in New York City and by October 9, similar demonstrations were either ongoing or had been held in 70 major cities and over 600 communities in the U.S. Internationally, over 900 cities are modeled themselves after Occupy Wall Street protests.

The opinions, beliefs, or views expressed in some these photographs are those of the Occupy Wall Street protesters and do not necessarily reflect my personal opinions, beliefs, or views.

These photographs are protected by United States and International Copyrights Laws. If you would like to use any of these images on your blog or news site, please contact me directly at: edsternphoto[at]gmail[dot]com

Title: IMG_3637
Description:
Brunocerous posted a photo:

Google: "We received a request from a local law enforcement agency to remove YouTube videos of police brutality."

Seems like the best way to avoid videos of police brutality on YouTube would be to stop police brutality.
___

[Felix] Rivera-Pitre, a former dancer who lives at the YMCA in Jamaica, Queens, said he was walking on William St. with other protesters when he "shot the cop a look."

"The cop just lunged at me full throttle and hit me on the left side of my face," he said. "It tore my earring out."

Title: 2011-11-01 - Occupy Vancouver Day 18
Description:
Suraky posted a photo:

There are probably as many tents as ever at the camp. With room made in places for fire safety in recent days by order of Vancouver's fire chief.

At 9am the camp is very quiet as crowds of 'sheeple' pass by to go to work. Someone has to pay for the electricity, portal potties for the camp, and the oversight of the police / fire department.

There's a few people awake in the camp but its not clear if there are actually a lot of people sleeping in the tents or not.

Title: General Strike in Oakland, CA: Port of Oakland
Description:
Rainforest Action Network posted a photo:

Rainforest Action Network joins the general strike in Oakland, California, Wednesday, November 2 with many thousands of peaceful protestors. "RAN believes the social, economic and environmental crises sweeping the planet are inter-related symptoms of the same root causes."

Less than three weeks after the Occupy movement began on Sept. 17, its “We Are the 99 Percent” message has exploded into a national rallying cry. We’ve been getting questions about why an environmental organization concerned with protecting forests, their inhabitants, and our climate would be supportive of a movement calling out the systems and institutions that maintain our country’s wealth inequality? Here’s why.

Rainforest Action Network joins the general strike in Oakland, California, Wednesday, November 2 with many thousands of peaceful protestors. "RAN believes the social, economic and environmental crises sweeping the planet are inter-related symptoms of the same root causes."

Less than three weeks after the Occupy movement began on Sept. 17, its “We Are the 99 Percent” message has exploded into a national rallying cry. We’ve been getting questions about why an environmental organization concerned with protecting forests, their inhabitants, and our climate would be supportive of a movement calling out the systems and institutions that maintain our country’s wealth inequality? Here’s why.

i'm in this park twice a day walking a pair of dogs who live nearby... it always seems very quiet in the encampment. but i guess they are hanging in there.

there's more tents than you can see in this picture, on the other side of the park. i just thought it made for a nice shot with city hall in the background.

Title: OWS - Control the Bankers
Description:
Ott!! posted a photo:

I met this guy at OWS and his main gripe is the paying of interest (usury). It's the way that bankers control your life. I believe he said that he lives in the NYC area and comes down on weekends to support the OWS movement. Later, it appeared he was interviewed by a news crew.

Title: the cry of the indigenous people is canada's shame .....
Description:
ana_lee_smith posted a photo:

On Saturday, Nov 12th, marking one month of occupation in St James Park, Occupy Toronto marched through the Financial District to Queen's Park in solidarity with First Nations Canadians, their native rights' struggles & land claims. Elders led the march with drums & sacred song. The young woman above, currently resident at the Occupy Toronto settlement, sings her ancestral song... seeming to have all the pain of her people's history written on her face.
.
.


short (2 mins) youtube video of Saturday's march, as it sets out along King Street in which you can hear the beautiful music of the First Nations contingent. (please click the blue link)

www.youtube.com/watch?v=dkvzar-6jFA&feature=player_em...
.
.
.
.
Thank you, all. The feedback & support you have so generously offered inspires me to keep going. The passionate faces of Occupy Toronto are irresistible, addictive even .....and they are many .... have posted others from Saturday's march behind this lead post ....easiest way to see them, if interested, is to go to the 'occupy toronto' set.

Title: the face of occupy toronto ..... valerie
Description:
ana_lee_smith posted a photo:

4 weeks / Saturday / Nov 5th 2011 / march to Queen's Park in solidarity with First Nations.

As we marched, Valerie & I discovered we had something very much in common. Her father was born in Liverpool & she was raised in Blackpool, a seaside town 55kms north of Liverpool, famous for its annual illuminations of billboard size storybook characters along the promenade strip. To go to 'Blackpool Lights' was a ritual that my Dad indulged his 5 children in every year..... we'd drive along the seafront road in a crawl of bottleneck traffic. A trip that never failed to enthrall *~*

Title: BC_111115_IMG_9920
Description:
OWS Photo posted a photo:

11/15/11 -- Zuccotti Park is occupied by NYPD after their midnight raid. They coupled with the Dept. of Sanitation to remove every bit of the encampment in garbage and dump trucks, and started cleaning the park with heavy machinery and privately contracted sanitation workers who doubled as security guards. In a role reversal, the Occupiers were on the outside as the NYPD attempted to hold the inside.
(photo by Brennan Cavanaugh; Creative Commons rules apply, please use responsibly)

Description:
OWS Photo posted a photo:

11/15/11 -- Zuccotti Park is occupied by NYPD after their midnight raid. They coupled with the Dept. of Sanitation to remove every bit of the encampment in garbage and dump trucks, and started cleaning the park with heavy machinery and privately contracted sanitation workers who doubled as security guards. In a role reversal, the Occupiers were on the outside as the NYPD attempted to hold the inside.

Title: 111128 Concentration of wealth a central issue
Description:
Ian Bunn posted a photo:

Frances Fox Piven the 78 year old US sociologist and political scientist has published an article on Aljazeera supportive of the Occupy Wall Street Movement. Piven states “… (OWS) movement has already made the concentration of wealth at the top of this society a central issue in US politics ... By making Wall Street its symbolic target and branding itself as a movement of the 99 per cent, OWS has redirected public attention to the issue of extreme inequality, which it has recast as, essentially, a moral problem … Economic policy, including tax cuts for the rich, subsidies and government protection … was shrouded in clouds of propaganda … Now, in what seems like no time at all, the fog has lifted and the topic on the table everywhere seems to be the morality of contemporary financial capitalism.

Title: Occupy Wall Street
Description:
Randy Le'Moine Photography posted a photo:

Occupy Wall Street (OWS) is an ongoing series of demonstrations initiated by the Canadian activist group Adbusters which began September 17, 2011 in Zuccotti Park, located in New York City's Wall Street financial district. The protests are against social and economic inequality, high unemployment, greed, as well as corruption, and the undue influence of corporations—particularly from the financial services sector—on government. The protesters' slogan We are the 99% refers to the growing difference in wealth in the U.S. between the wealthiest 1% and the rest of the population.

Title: White Shirt
Description:
de-lineation posted a photo:

I took this shot on the 17th of last month, on the 2nd month anniversary of OWS. I'm not quite sure why this white shirt was standing up on this legde, but apparently he thought it gave him a better view of the street where the march was scheduled to walk. Sadly, he was on the wrong street. The only view he had was of the random protestor on his or her way to Foley Square.

Description:
raincoaster posted a photo:

I forget this fellow's real name, but he was very nice. You can also tell a lot about people from their dogs, and his was bold, friendly, and well-mannered. This is one of the people at OV who had been homeless; he said he was one of the complicated ones to house, because he wouldn't give up his dog, but on the last day of the VAG tent city, City of Vancouver workers found him an awesome place right in downtown to live and he was very happy there.

Title: Die Farben Deiner Stadt *
Description:
Sterneck posted a photo:

*


Streetart - Frankfurt am Main
Fotos : Wolfgang Sterneck & Friends
wwww.sterneck.net

*

WELCHE FARBE HAT DEINE STADT ?

Hast Du schon einmal die Werbeplakate
in einer Fußgängerzone gezählt?

Oder all die Kameras,
die Dich unablässig überwachen?

Doch auch in den durchgestylten Shopping-Zonen
finden sich kreative Zeichen einer anderen Welt,
fernab von Kommerz, Konsum und Kontrolle.

Da lächelt Dich auf einer Betonwand ein Gesicht an,
ohne Dir etwas verkaufen zu wollen.

Du entdeckst zwischen Werbefassaden einen Stencil,
der die Lust auf Veränderung spiegelt.

Und Du liest eine Botschaft, die Dich daran erinnert,
wonach Du Dich wirklich sehnst ...

Diese Kunst in den Straßen nimmt sich
die Stadt zurück und eröffnet Freiräume.
Sie ist Gestaltung, Anregung und
Vision zugleich.

Wolfgang Sterneck
www.sterneck.net
- * -



*

Attached is a jpg of our finished poster both walking poster and standup, as an example of how the template can be used.  Any politician's face can be pasted into the face area.

Title: Occupy Salt Lake City Oral History Interview - Stewart Thorpe

The Occupy SLC Oral History Project is being conducted by the University of Utah's American West Center and J. Willard Marriott Library in order to record the thoughts, beliefs and emotions of the people behind this grassroots movement.

Title: Club Mighty Mike 30-Oct-2011 Occupy Boston
Description:
Club Mighty Mike, Occupy Boston 30-Oct-2011

Boston got hit hardest with winter weather first, as you can see they were smuggling pallets in at night and setting up a plank system to keep people out of the mud. They had a gentlemen from the military who had obviously been through some cold weather training at the GA explaining how not to die in the snow at night.

Everyone who liked the idea of 'winterization working groups' needs to thank Occupy Boston.

Description:

Description:

Title: We saw something, ~Sept 17-20th Occupy Wall Street NYC, NY
Description:
This was one of the first signs I really liked and towards the end of it, it remained one of my favorites.

For anyone who see's this outside of the USA, Homeland Security has plastered signs all over the country informing citizens to report any suspicious behavior by telling them 'If you see something, say something'.

Title: Occupy Salt Lake City Oral History Interview - John Netto
Description:
An interview with John Netto about his support of the Occupy SLC movement by Michael McLane on April 24, 2012. 

The Occupy SLC Oral History Project is being conducted by the University of Utah's American West Center and J. Willard Marriott Library in order to record the thoughts, beliefs and emotions of the people behind this grassroots movement.

http://www.awc.utah.edu/

Title: | #OccupyWallStreet |
Description:
SOBPhotography posted a photo:

On this date last year a tweet went out;

"7/15/11 11:04 AM
Sept 17. Wall St. Bring Tent. adbusters.org/blogs/adbuster… #OCCUPYWALLSTREET"

two months after this tweet was sent a couple hundred people answered the call and converged on Wall Street. This sparked an international movement that saw occupations spring up in every major city in the United States and around the world. Since this tweet thousands of hard working Americans and citizens round the world have been arrested or injured at the hands of our own governments, yet despite the States best efforts to suppress the movement and silence the majority the movement keeps growing and getting louder.

The call has gone out once again to Occupy Wall Street on the one year anniversary of the occupations beginning. You're not going to find this story in the main stream media so I suggest you do a little digging of your own on the internet to find out the real story. Just remember, the LIBOR scandal is the largest banking scandal in history undoubtedly involving the CEO's of all the major banking institutions yet our own media, CNN, FOX, MSNBC and ABC have dedicated a mere 12 minutes combined covering the story and investigation. The NYT's is reporting that the U.S. Justice department is seeking criminal charges against traders. Good you say but that's not enough, they need to go after the architects of this scandal but that won't happen because as stated earlier this criminal act had to include the involvement of government officials and the CEO's of the banks that carried out the price fixing.

Title: _DSC6640
Description:
Adam Ebihara Photography posted a photo:

9.17.12
NYC

#S17 OWS First Year Anniversary. The arrests started quickly with these taking place just before 8 a.m. at the very early stages of the march. The protestor backing into the van was arrested. The gentleman to the left is retired Episcopal Bishop George Packard. His arrest was the first that I personally saw directly after he addressed an assembly across the street from Liberty Park. He marched briefly & was quickly detained. Several members of "Veterans for Peace" were among the first arrested as well. [My account is anecdotal & not verified.]

Title: | Occupy Sandy |
Description:
SOBPhotography posted a photo:

Residents and activists of Staten Island and the Far Rockaways protested outside Mayor Bloomberg's residence on Saturday night demanding that the city speed up recovery efforts and to also bring attention to the fact that there are still thousands of families living in mold infested homes without heat or electricity. Although the protesters were very vocal they were peaceful and yet the NYPD managed to find some reason to arrest demonstrators.

Title: Archivo 15M show in New York City
Description:
1. English / 2. Espanol
http://archivosol15m.wordpress.com/

Posters of the 15M Puerta del Sol Encampment on Display in New York City.
Published: January 10, 2013 | Author: archivosol15m | Filed under: Exhibitions and Media, News | Leave a comment »
The bookstore Bluestockings hosts the Exhibition Archive 15M. A small sample of printed reproductions of posters and banners along with some pictures of the 15M movement camping in Puerta del Sol in Madrid, will be exhibited from January 9 to February 15 at the bookstore feminist / anarchist Bluestockings in New York, 172 Allen St. has been prepared by the committee of Madrid 15M File, which from the start had the task of collecting all the documentary material generated by the protest movement that continues to work even though the original of this exhibition are still hostages inside the building which housed the Social Center Casablanca, evicted last September 19, 2012. With this exhibition we aim to strengthen ties with movements inspired by the same feeling in the whole world.
This show is available to travel in the U.S.A.

in collaboration with “House Magic” information project – https://sites.google.com/site/housemagicbfc/

Pancartas de la Acampada de Sol son expuestas en Nueva York.
Publicado: enero 10, 2013 | Autor: archivosol15m | Archivado en: Exposiciones y prensa, Noticias | Deja un comentario »
La librería Bluestockings acoge la Exposición 15M Archive. Una pequeña muestra de reproducciones impresas de carteles y pancartas junto con algunas fotografías de la Acampada del movimiento 15M en la Puerta del Sol de Madrid, serán expuestas desde el 9 de enero al 15 de febrero en la librería feminista / anarquista Bluestockings de Nueva York, 172 Allen St. Ha sido preparada por la comisión de Archivo 15M de Madrid, que desde el primer momento asumió la tarea de recoger todo el material documental generado por este movimiento de protesta y que sigue trabajando a pesar de que los originales de esta exposición se encuentran todavía secuestrados dentro del edificio que albergaba el Centro Social Casablanca, desalojado el pasado 19 de septiembre del 2012. Con esta exposición pretendemos estrechar lazos con movimientos inspirados por una misma sensibilidad en todo el mundo.
Este programa está disponible para viajar en el U.S.A.

en colaboración con el “House Magic” proyecto de información – https://sites.google.com/site/housemagicbfc/

Title: An occupier raises his fist in protest as Philadelphia PD bike unit kettles and arrests entire march during Occupy's National Gatherine
Description:
juliacreinhart posted a photo:

A bike unit of Philadelphia's Police Department kettles and arrest an entire march of Occupy Wall Street protesters during their national gathering in the city over the July 4th weekend. The group had marched through the city peacefully, but on an unauthorized route, when they were pushed into a side alley and arrested.
